title: ～ばいい — you just have to ～, it is fine to just ～
summary: Gives advice or says that one action is enough: “just ～ and it's fine / you should ～.” It attaches to the ば-form of a verb. It is used for suggestions, instructions, and giving someone relief by showing a simple way.

patterns.form: 動詞ば形 ＋ いい／いいです
patterns.gloss: ば-form + いい: 聞けばいい (just ask)
Group 1: u → e + ば (聞く → 聞けば). Group 2: る → れば (見る → 見れば). する → すれば, 来る → 来れば

body.p: ～ばいい tells the listener the one thing they need to do. 困ったときは私に聞けばいいです means that asking me is enough. It is a friendly way to show a simple solution and also works as advice.
～たらいい has almost the same meaning and is a little softer in advice. In the negative, ～なければいい is rare; use ～ないほうがいい instead. To a superior, avoid it as a direct instruction and use ～ていただければ.

examples.ja: 困（こま）ったときは私（わたし）に聞（き）けばいいです。
examples.romaji: Komatta toki wa watashi ni kikeba ii desu.
examples.tr: When you're in trouble, you can just ask me.

examples.ja: 道（みち）が分（わ）からなければ、地図（ちず）を見（み）ればいい。
examples.romaji: Michi ga wakarenakereba, chizu o mireba ii.
examples.tr: If you don't know the way, you can just look at a map.

examples.ja: 疲（つか）れたのなら、少（すこ）し休（やす）めばいいですよ。
examples.romaji: Tsukareta no nara, sukoshi yasumeba ii desu yo.
examples.tr: If you're tired, you should just rest a little.

pitfalls: Use the ば-form: 聞けばいい, not 聞くばいい.
To a superior, it can sound like an order. Soften it, e.g. ～ていただければ結構です.
